- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., -0.50 to -0.67); model tends to overshoot into bullish territory.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70 or below) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays mean reversion, especially after strong upward moves; true prices revert faster than forecasted.
- When sentiment is mildly negative (-0.30 to -0.40), model tends to overreact with upward bias — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of forecasted value.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts mid-to-late period prices, especially after 10–15 days — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction for days 11–20.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust — apply a 0.3–0.7% upward correction to avoid underestimating rebound.
